hints.title: Consecutive Value Grouping via Row Offset
hints.text: A sequence of consecutive numbers has a constant difference between each log_id and its row number.

hints.title: Window Function Island Partition
hints.text: Calculate log_id - row_number() over (order by log_id) to assign a uniform group identifier to every continuous sequence.

hints.title: Continuous Ranges Blueprint
hints.text: with NumberedLogs as (select log_id, log_id - row_number() over (order by log_id) as grp from Logs) select min(log_id) as start_id, max(log_id) as end_id from NumberedLogs group by grp order by start_id.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH NumberedLogs AS (
    SELECT log_id, log_id - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY log_id) AS grp
    FROM Logs
)
SELECT MIN(log_id) AS start_id, MAX(log_id) AS end_id
FROM NumberedLogs
GROUP BY grp
ORDER BY start_id;
```

variables: N: number of records in Logs table
complexity.notes: Window ranking and grouping by constant delta executes in linear-logarithmic time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Self-joins across gaps require quadratic comparisons to connect endpoints.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Row number subtraction forms island groups in a single scan.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Classic gaps-and-islands pattern using ROW_NUMBER() difference.
